summary: Verified WBS access control fix: project leads (role=resource, linked as project_lead_id) can now perform WBS write operations on projects they lead, while non-lead resources are correctly rejected with 403 and admins retain full access. 12/12 backend tests passed.
critical_code_review_comments: wbs.py is ~1530 lines - consider splitting into wbs_crud.py, wbs_ai.py, wbs_baseline.py, wbs_summary.py for maintainability.

_require_admin_or_project_lead() helper is only defined in routes/wbs.py; if other resource-scoped routes (allocations, timesheets approval, etc.) need the same 'lead can also edit' pattern, consider moving it to auth/dependencies.py as a shared FastAPI dependency factory (e.g., require_admin_or_project_lead(project_id) using Depends) — cleaner than manual awaits in each handler.

All 11 endpoints exercised in tests/test_wbs_project_lead.py — POST/PUT/DELETE tasks, recalculate-dates, project set-baseline, task set-baseline, complete-milestone, sync-dates-from-wbs, plus non-lead 403 checks. rca of the issue: Original bug: all WBS write endpoints used require_admin so project leads (role=resource) hit 403. Fix moved them to get_current_user + _require_admin_or_project_lead() which calls user_leads_project() — admin/super_admin bypass, otherwise the user's linked resource _id must equal project.project_lead_id. Verified end-to-end.
